pencereler.0-5: A gas pipeline exploded under a California neighbourhood. Fire destroyed dozens of homes, and
pencereler.5-12: eight people were killed. The pipe section had been installed in 1956. Company records said it was seamless. In
pencereler.12-20: reality, it had a badly made weld. When pressure rose, the weld tore open. Escaping gas ignited in a huge fireball. Operators
pencereler.20-30: then had to verify records and pressure-test old lines.

bulgular: 12-20s: no central mystery or problem is posed

segmentler.metin: The San Bruno gas pipeline exploded under a residential neighbourhood.
It took only a pressure rise on a pipe with a defective weld.
So how could a pressure rise on a pipe with a defective weld do this?
The answer is rupture of a pipeline section with a defective seam weld installed in 1956 — and it is why US pipeline operators had to verify records and pressure-test old lines.
